object_description: two-storey compact block organised around a central inner courtyard with a sunken sports hall
geometry_property: roof used as a break area
design_condition: the building is precisely positioned on the alignment of the neighbouring hall, forming a street space read from facade to facade, with the green strip removed along its whole length

positive: The urban positioning is impressive and precisely integrated into the site
The building stands out from the neighbouring hall and leaves room for a future swimming pool
A two-storey compact structure appears from the large avenue
Dispensing with the second tree row creates a generous open street space understood from facade to facade
The green promenade contrasts with the urban promenade
The inner courtyard with trees, planting and paths creates an atmospheric and easily usable outdoor space
A diverse spectrum of spatially, atmospherically and functionally convincing open spaces
The separation of functions has been implemented consistently and naturally
Student areas are gathered on one floor with sufficient pre-zones and the patient and laboratory wing on another
The arrangement allows a good flow of patients with carefully chosen room proportions
Circulation around the attractive inner courtyard allows very good orientation and creates varied meeting zones
The spiral main staircase creates a generous and logical connection across all floors
The courtyard serves as a central garden that can be opened up and used with the cafeteria
Clear structures allow orientation with visual connections and optimal networking between user groups
The functions present themselves to the outside as a single unit with a homogeneous facade
Large window openings give the necessary daylight and protection from direct sun
The cafeteria is ideally located at the courtyard and can be perceived as the centre of the department
Delivery and internal operations are well organised
Offices are sensibly located and well lit, and open-space offices can easily be converted into group offices
The sports hall and adjoining rooms are well connected and sensibly organised
Bicycle parking is sensibly arranged and convincingly connected by additional entrances
The claim to accommodate all functions in a large homogeneous volume is particularly convincing
Convincing urban design, structural logic and operational organisation with clear spatial structures
negative: Separation of the sports hall for external use is not recognisable and separate renting is not possible
The courtyard gives the sports hall only indirect light
The use of the roof as a sports break area should be reconsidered
The lowered lecture hall is only accessible in the middle of the grading, preventing disabled access for lecturers
The entrance is not easily recognisable from the large avenue
There is no connection between the cafeteria and the western courtyard garden
The uses are not recognisable from the outside
The incidence of light in the sports hall must be checked to prevent grazing light
Summer heat insulation is not sufficiently explained and it is unclear whether the windows can be opened
The load-bearing construction is only partially legible and can be costed only to a limited extent
Courtyard glazing and the U-shaped attic create a large facade envelope area with corresponding cost implications
High costs are also expected for the inner glazing and the used roofs
